course.title: Uncertainty, Interpretability and Model Validation
course.tagline: Produce the evidence an independent validator needs: calibrated probabilities, intervals with guarantees, honest explanations and a fit-for-use decision
course.description: Participants produce the evidence an independent validator needs about a trained model: whether its probabilities can be trusted, how wide its errors are, what drives its predictions, where it stops working and whom it fails. For Mizan Community Lending, a fictional microfinance lender, they repair calibration, wrap models in conformal intervals and prediction sets, test coverage by subgroup and under shift, show where explanations mislead, tabulate subgroup error and write a validation report against a published checklist. Fairness mitigation and documentation are DS-309.
course.audience: Specialists. Analysts and data scientists who have completed the level 200 set or can show equivalent work: an analysis or model they built, validated and can explain.
prerequisites: DS-204 Machine Learning for Tabular Data: Baselines and Validation
DS-301 Regression and Generalised Linear Modelling
Trains and cross-validates a gradient-boosted classifier
course.format_note: Intensive: 4 teaching days of four sessions and a capstone day, with guided pre-work and a tracked follow-up task

outcomes.text: Measure calibration with proper scores and reliability diagrams, recalibrate, and report the effect by subgroup, given a trained default classifier and a held-out set
outcomes.evidence: before-and-after diagrams, Brier scores and a subgroup table

outcomes.text: Implement conformal intervals and prediction sets and test coverage overall, by subgroup and under simulated shift, given a loss-amount regression and a three-grade risk classifier
outcomes.evidence: a table of target against achieved coverage with widths and set sizes

outcomes.text: Apply permutation, accumulated-local-effect and Shapley-value explanations and test their stability across refits, given a boosted model with two correlated income features
outcomes.evidence: an explanation report with a stability panel and one documented misleading result

outcomes.text: Diagnose why a model degrades on a later batch from slice metrics, coverage loss and changed explanations, given a shifted batch with a seeded cause
outcomes.evidence: a memo naming the cause and an action

outcomes.text: Audit a model package for conceptual soundness, outcome performance and monitoring readiness and decide whether it is fit for use, given another team's model, documentation and data, with a reporting checklist and the national bias guide
outcomes.evidence: a validation report with rated findings, subgroup gaps and conditions of use, defended before a panel

case_study.name: Mizan Community Lending
case_study.summary: Mizan Community Lending is a fictional microfinance lender whose credit analytics team hands its model package Amana (a default model, a three-grade model and a loss model) to the model risk team for independent validation. Participants are that team: on 50,000 synthetic applications, a held-out set and a later batch from 2025, they test the package's claims, repair calibration, wrap the models in conformal intervals and prediction sets, test what the explanations say and how stable they are, find the seeded cause of a decline, and decide whether Amana is fit for use and under which conditions. All data is synthetic and generated with a fixed seed.

sessions.label: Session 4

days.label: Capstone
days.title: Capstone: an independent validation
days.subtitle: Eight-minute panel defence of a validation report, then four minutes of questions in which the panel picks one finding to rerun

capstone.summary: An independent validation of another participant's or a course model package, in a public repository whose README reports calibration, coverage, explanation stability, subgroup findings and a fit-for-use decision; eight-minute panel defence plus questions
capstone.submission: A link to a public GitHub repository holding the validation notebooks, the run logs, and a README that reports calibration, coverage, explanation stability, subgroup findings and the fit-for-use decision
